num_screens.title: Your monthly take-home
num_screens.purpose: The one income number the plan cannot do without. Exact first; AA salary detection prefills it when present.
num_screens.question: What lands in your account every month, after tax?
num_screens.hint: Take-home, not CTC. Bonuses go under other income.
num_screens.suggestion: You said about Rs 17.5 L a year earlier; roughly Rs 1.2 L a month after tax? (from R03; change it if that is off)
num_screens.readback: one lakh twenty thousand a month, about Rs 14.4 L a year
ladder: Fetched from Account Aggregator: the salary credit detected on a fixed day
Your salary slip or your bank app
midpoint fills the field, tagged approx
num_screens.plausibility: take-home against the R03 household income band
logic: Salary detection from AA bank transactions: a recurring credit on a fixed day, shown as a suggestion the user confirms (spec v0.1 D05).
states: AA-fed: the v0.1 rows (average monthly credits and debits over twelve months) sit above the question; manual: rows absent
dev: Transaction categorisation is V2; V1 shows totals and the detected salary only (spec v0.1 D05).

ladder: Your partner's salary slip or bank app
A band for this field (household take-home)
midpoint fills the field, tagged approx

num_screens.title: Rental income

num_screens.hint: What lands in the account, after the society and the agent take their share.

num_screens.title: Other income
num_screens.purpose: Business, freelance, bonus, anything else. Band first; regular or lumpy.
num_screens.question: Anything else that comes in? Business, freelance, a bonus, family support.
num_screens.hint: Regular or lumpy, either is fine; say which.

ladder: Last year's total, from your tax return or your bank app
midpoint fills the field, tagged approx
logic: Regular or lumpy: two chips under the amount set income_regularity (spec v0.1 D05); lumpy income is averaged over the year in the cashflow.

num_screens.title: Total monthly outgoings
num_screens.purpose: Everything that goes out in a month, as one number first. The surplus updates live under it.
num_screens.question: Roughly, how much goes out every month, everything included?
num_screens.hint: Rent, EMIs, school, groceries, help, subscriptions, the lot. One number; the split comes next.
num_screens.suggestion: From what you told me about saving (R05), about Rs ___ a month goes out. Fix it if that is off.
num_screens.readback: one lakh thirty thousand a month, about Rs 15.7 L a year
ladder: Fetched from Account Aggregator: average monthly debits over twelve months
Your bank app: last month's debits
midpoint fills the field, tagged approx
num_screens.plausibility: outgoings against take-home (D05a) and the R05 savings rate; EMIs from D03 against 30 percent of take-home
logic: Live surplus line under the input: take-home minus outgoings, updating as the user types.
EMIs from D03 show read-only inside the total once known; the surplus re-shows after D03 (spec v0.1 D06).
states: Deficit: the surplus line turns into the deficit line, copy per the React: you are running a deficit budget, income or expenses need a re-look; the plan still builds
dev: The Pets card on D01 (row 8 note) adds a recurring expense line inside the fixed bucket on D06b.

questions.text: How many financial dependants do you have?
options: None
More than 4
Very secure & stable
Secure & stable
Not very stable
Highly unstable & irregular

questions.text: Which of the following statements would best describe your level of knowledge as an investor?
options: I am a proficient investor & understand nuances of all products in the market
I understand & invest in mutual funds regularly but not aware of how to analyse them
I understand only basic products like fixed deposits, gold etc
I am not very familiar with investment options and financial planning

questions.text: How would you describe your overall income status?
options: I save more than 30% of my take-home salary every month
I put aside at least 10% of my take-home salary every month in savings
My Provident Fund and other employment benefits are my only source of savings
Just about manage to make ends meet; no monthly savings

questions.text: Assume you had an investment portfolio worth Rs.100,000. If, due to market conditions, your portfolio fell to Rs.75,000 within a short period, say a month, would you (If your portfolio has experienced a drop like this, chose the answer that corresponds to your actual behavior)
options: Invest more funds to lower your average investment price
Hold the investment and sell nothing, expecting performance to improve
Sell a portion of your portfolio to cut your losses and reinvest into more secure investment sectors
Sell all of the investments. I do not intend to take risks.

questions.text: Which of the following would best describe your investment goal?
options: I am willing to take adequate risks in some part of my portfolio for better wealth creation
I am willing to tolerate only some downside upto 10-20% of portfolio
I want regular income only. Not looking for wealth creation.
Safety first. I do not want to lose any money at all.

questions.text: The table below shows the highest one-year gain & one-year loss on three different investment options. Given the potential gain or loss in any one year, where would you invest your money?
options: Investment D
Investment C
Investment B
Investment A
